source.author: verg
source.text: Vestibulum ante ipsum primoque in limine Pyrrhus exsultat, telis et luce coruscus aëna; qualis ubi in lucem coluber mala gramina pastus frigida sub terra tumidum quem bruma tegebat, nunc, positis novus exuviis nitidusque iuventa, lubrica convolvit sublato pectore terga arduus ad solem, et linguis micat ore trisulcis.
source.text_original: Vestibulum ante ipsum primoque in limine Pyrrhus / exsultat, telis et luce coruscus aëna; / qualis ubi in lucem coluber mala gramina pastus / frigida sub terra tumidum quem bruma tegebat, / nunc, positis novus exuviis nitidusque iuventa, / lubrica convolvit sublato pectore terga / arduus ad solem, et linguis micat ore trisulcis.
source.text_english: In the entrance hall, right on the threshold itself, Pyrrhus leaps forward, flashing with weapons and bronze light; like when a snake, fed on harmful grasses, whom winter had covered in the cold earth, now, having shed its skin, fresh and shining in youth, writhes its slippery coils, raising its breast and towering up his back toward the sun, and his mouth flickers with triple-forked tongues.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Ecce per obliqui rapidum compendia montis ductor avens laetusque dolis agnoscit Acastum horrentem iaculis et parmae luce coruscum.
reuse.text_original: Ecce per obliqui rapidum compendia montis / ductor avens laetusque dolis agnoscit Acastum / horrentem iaculis et parmae luce coruscum.
reuse.text_english: Look, by the steep shortcuts of the slanting mountain, the leader, eager and glad at the stratagem, recognizes Acastus, bristling with spears and flashing with the sheen of his round shield.
